name: Rule script
description: `esoi check` runs every registered rule group, the numbered rule modules, over the tree, registry and results, with strict mode, disabled ids, plugins and waivers; each finding is led by its rule id and path and says its next action.
advantages: One runner for every rule, fast, runs before commit and in tests; a plugin adds a rule without touching it; enforced in code and named by id and path. Selected because: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
disadvantages: A custom tool to maintain; the reason for a rule is not recorded beside it.

name: Rules as linter plugins
description: Runs each rule as a plugin of a linter people already use, so violations show in the editor and in existing hooks.
advantages: Reuses tools and editor integration that contributors already have.
disadvantages: A linter reads one file at a time, so rules that compare the records with the code across files do not fit.

name: Rules in prose
description: The rules written in the standard document and followed by whoever read it, with code review as the check.
advantages: Costs nothing to write or change.
disadvantages: Followed by whoever read them and broken by the next agent.
